solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unfriendly daughter isn't accepting thanks

indicators.note: the word for thanks is taken into the middle of isn't, as a host accepts a guest

parts.note: written without its apostrophe
TA is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A cold daughter refuses to say thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A distant manner is aloof and cool, a close synonym of unfriendly.

clue.text: Appropriate behaviour from Italian writer caught in snare, perhaps

indicators.note: the writer is trapped inside the drum word

parts.note: a snare is a kind of drum
Umberto Eco, the Italian novelist

explanation.surface: An Italian author gets caught in a trap, as a matter of good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snare' suggests a trap, but here it is a snare drum.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is propriety and good taste in conduct.

clue.text: Drama series on TV that provides place to air views

parts.note: a soap opera is a long-running drama series
the box is informal for television

explanation.surface: A TV soap gives people a platform for their opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: A soapbox is an improvised platform for public speakers, originally a crate for soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on one's soapbox means holding forth on one's opinions in public.

clue.text: Final pronouncement from abroad, i.e. ultimatum

indicators.note: the answer is taken from the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A foreign power issues its last word in the form of an ultimatum.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell, the last thing said on parting.

clue.text: Time to study economist's revolutionary form of punishment

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
John Stuart Mill, the economist and philosopher

explanation.surface: An economist's revolutionary ideas about punishment get time for study.
explanation.walkthrough: The treadmill was a Victorian prison punishment in which inmates walked on a turning wheel, hence revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners were sentenced to tread the rotating wheel as a penal labour.

clue.text: Resistance, in part, is hard for people in these islands

definitions.note: plural noun sense: the British as a people

indicators.note: the resistance letter sits in the word for part

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A wartime-sounding remark that the islanders' resistance movement is partly tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: The inhabitants of Great Britain and its surrounding isles are collectively called the British.

clue.text: Man, for example, one quietly sleeping?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that sleeping is read as in bed, so the other pieces are put inside it

parts.note: sleeping means being in bed, which gives the word for bed as the container
I is the Roman numeral for one
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps, is someone dozing silently.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleeping is read as 'in bed', which both supplies BED and puts the other pieces inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, so a man is one example of a two-footed animal.

clue.text: Like rebels occupying South, needing immediate attention

parts.note: occupying a place is being in it
S is the compass abbreviation for south
urgent means needing immediate attention

explanation.surface: Rebels seizing the south pose an urgent problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurgent describes those in revolt against authority, as rebels are.

clue.text: For example, an old king I overturned a long, long time ago

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole string is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of toppling an ancient king in the distant past.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is the prehistoric era after the Bronze Age, millennia in the past.

clue.text: Expert's tautology about high temperature

parts.note: a tautology repeats itself, so this is a statement that heat is heat, split as two words with an apostrophe s; read whole it is a word for an ace

explanation.surface: A specialist states the obvious about a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as HOT'S HOT, a statement that says the same thing twice, which is also a word for an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is a highly skilled, successful person, informally an ace.

clue.text: Wine goblet found in church by daughter of Oxford dean

parts.note: Alice Liddell, the girl behind Alice in Wonderland, was the daughter of Henry Liddell, Dean of Christ Church, Oxford

explanation.surface: A communion cup turns up in an Oxford church, brought by the dean's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland for Alice Liddell, whose father was Dean of Christ Church, Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a stemmed cup, especially the one used for communion wine.

clue.text: Finish training as fighter and faint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to graduate from military training

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a recruit collapsing at the passing-out parade; the two halves are separate senses of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both graduating from a military academy and collapsing unconscious.

clue.text: Fixed book with editor and made a comeback

parts.note: a book fixed with a new binding has been rebound

explanation.surface: A publisher repairs a volume with an editor's help and makes a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebound is to bounce back or recover after a setback, a synonym of returning.

clue.text: Achieve some basic education with a head

parts.note: R stands for one of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
each means per person, as in ten pounds a head

explanation.surface: Getting basic schooling to every pupil is an achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic, so one R is some basic education.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a goal is to attain or achieve it.

clue.text: One's automatically fired, as a principle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... gun, the first fully automatic machine gun
second meaning: a short statement of a general rule

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like someone sacked on principle; the first half is the Maxim machine gun, which fires automatically.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a succinct rule of conduct; the Maxim gun was named after inventor Hiram Maxim.

clue.text: Life's made complicated for a poet

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are muddled up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's life has been made difficult for a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: John Masefield was British Poet Laureate from 1930 to 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: Masefield, author of Sea-Fever, held the post of Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Addition after changing sides? That's not fair

indicators.note: right is swapped for left, so the R in the word for addition becomes an L

parts.note: an increment is an increase or addition

explanation.surface: A political defector's extra perk is called unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing sides here means right becomes left: R becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement weather is stormy or harsh, the opposite of fair weather.

clue.text: Cold American, pale and afraid of being shot

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
AMER is the abbreviation for American
ashy means ash-coloured, pale

explanation.surface: A chilly, pale American is terrified of being gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire; here it means photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera-shy person dislikes being photographed, and a photo is a shot.

clue.text: City played in London initially in 2009

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the holy city in Israel and Palestine
second meaning: Jez Butterworth's play, which premiered at the Royal Court in London in 2009

explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letters signal, but it means first staged: Butterworth's play opened in London in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the ancient Middle Eastern capital and to a celebrated modern stage play.

clue.text: Make fool of sailor on a ship

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fool of a sailor aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackass is literally a male donkey and figuratively a stupid person.

clue.text: Pragmatic approach is needed in kingdom

indicators.note: the word is is required to sit inside the kingdom word

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom

explanation.surface: A practical outlook is required for governing a kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is facing facts and acting practically rather than idealistically.

clue.text: Minimal temperature I predict for mountainous country

parts.note: the smallest piece of temperature, its first letter T
to bet is to predict, as in I bet it rains

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster expects freezing conditions in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibet sits on the high Himalayan plateau, often called the roof of the world.

clue.text: Composer attacked by insects, crossing river

indicators.note: the bitten word stretches across the river letter, holding it

parts.note: midges or mosquitoes leave you bitten
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A composer gets eaten alive by midges while crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was the English composer of Peter Grimes.

clue.text: Mug putting most of capital into trust fund ultimately

indicators.note: with into, the shortened capital is placed inside the two final letters
with putting, the capital goes inside the letters of trust fund
the last letter of each of trust and fund
all but the final letter of the capital

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey

explanation.surface: A sucker sinks most of his capital into a trust fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a gullible victim of the scheme, but it is a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, often of pewter with a handle.

clue.text: Banter husband accepted in eatery

indicators.note: the husband letter is let into the eatery word

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café

explanation.surface: A husband swaps jokes after being let into a café.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is a cheap, no-frills British café.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff as a noun is light-hearted teasing, a synonym of banter.

clue.text: Command one army corps, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the corps letters go in the word for a manner of speaking

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking or enunciating
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: An officer is told to command a corps, metaphorically speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a homophone signal or a figure of speech; here it is the container DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction is an instruction or order, close in meaning to a command.

clue.text: Work that's personal, penning that heartless song

indicators.note: the home-improvement letters enclose the heartless word, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: DIY is do-it-yourself, work you do personally

indicators.note: the word that with its middle letters removed

explanation.surface: A personal work encloses a heartless little song.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditty is a short, simple song or verse.

clue.text: Kind of butterfly often found in list

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., a butterfly with a white ...-shaped mark
second meaning: the punctuation mark separating items in a list

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a butterfly on a collector's list; the second meaning is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The comma is both a European butterfly named for a wing marking and the punctuation separating listed items.

clue.text: A river that is extremely short of water

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A river that has almost dried up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid means dry, lacking rainfall; the superlative is the driest.

clue.text: Old woman absorbed by Hindu scripture in Asian island

indicators.note: the mother word is taken inside the scripture word

parts.note: a sutra is an aphorism or collection of them in Hindu literature
ma is mother, informally the old woman

explanation.surface: An elderly woman engrossed in holy texts on an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian isle in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Influence holding protest back, sooner or later

indicators.note: the say word holds the reversed protest word inside it

parts.note: to have a say is to have influence

indicators.note: the protest word is read backwards

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Holding a protest will bring influence eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Someday means at an unspecified future time, as does eventually.

clue.text: Final instalment of pay, deserved and desired

indicators.note: the last letter of the word pay

parts.note: earned means deserved, as in well-earned rest

explanation.surface: A worker who longed for the last payment had earned it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have yearned is to have longed for something, a synonym of wanted.
